description.narrative:
Project outcomes: Stakeholder Effects - Increased Access to Climate Finance especially for industrial decarbonization. The Fund will increase access to finance across SEA and SA for industrial and infrastructure projects, enabling sustainable economic growth as the region transitions to a low-carbon economy. The Fund will focus primarily on industrial decarbonization (approximately 45-55% of the Fund). Climate financing may also stimulate innovation in manufacturing industries, fostering the development and deployment of cutting-edge technologies such as green hydrogen, Carbon Capture, Utilization, and Storage (CCUS), electrification, sustainable aviation fuel, and circular economy practices. The Fund will offer customized solutions tailored to the specific needs of at least 10 investments with individual investments ranging between US$25 million and US$75 million and an average investment size of US$50 million.
Assessment of Contribution to Market Creation: Sustainability. IFC anticipates that the Project will foster sustainability in Emerging Asia, specifically SEA (80% of investments) by demonstrating mechanisms to draw long term financing for industrial decarbonization, including sectors transitioning to low-carbon growth and emerging decarbonization technology solutions. Through demonstration and replication, the Project is expected to help crowd-in private capital for climate financing activities through new climate-focused debt funds. Through this intervention, IFC anticipates the Project will strengthen the climate finance market in SEA by demonstrating the viability of a debt fund focused on industrial decarbonization, incorporating innovative financing structures and risk mitigation tools. The Project aims to deepen market functioning by positioning EM debt as a competitive asset class and mobilizing institutional capital, especially insurance providers, that are relatively new to the low-carbon transition space specifically in SEA.

The proposed IFC investment consists of up to US$50 million equity subscriptions into limited partnership interests of the Emerging Asia Infrastructure Credit Fund (EAICF or the Fund), a US$750 million target blended finance fund. The proposed investment comprises: (i) up to US$40 million into a senior tranche for IFC's own account; (ii) up to US$5 million into a junior tranche for IFCs own account; and (iii) up to US$5 million into a junior tranche, to be supported by Frontier Opportunities Fund (FOF) as described in the Blended Finance Section. The Fund will provide senior, mezzanine and subordinated debt to support the transition of private sector borrowers, including in the industrial, and decarbonization technologies sectors, towards low-carbon growth. Also, the Fund will have a primary focus on Southeast Asia (SEA) (80% of capital commitments), with the remaining allocation potentially targeted to South Asia (SA). Emerging Asia Infrastructure Credit Fund GP S.a r.l., a Luxemburg private limited company managed by BlackRock Financial Management Inc. (BlackRock), will serve as the general partner of the Fund (the General Partner).
